ringing.meaning: making a clear loud sound, like a bell.

senses.meaning: making a clear loud sound, like a bell.
senses.here: His boots make a loud clear sound on the stone floor.
senses.example: He went to her, his boots ringing on the stone floor.

rolling.meaning: rising and falling gently, like waves

senses.meaning: rising and falling gently, like waves
senses.here: A rolling plain: land rising and falling gently, stretched as far as the eye could see.
senses.example: To the east the land was lower, the ground flattening to a rolling plain that stretched away as far as the eye could see.

senses.meaning: Fast boats on a river.
senses.here: River runners come and go; fast boats on the river.
senses.example: Deepwater fishing boats and river runners came and went, ferrymen poled back and forth across the Blackwater Rush, trading galleys unloaded goods from Braavos and Pentos and Lys.

senses.meaning: a cold dish of greens.
senses.here: Salads of sweetgrass and spinach are served.
senses.example: Salads of sweetgrass and spinach and plums, sprinkled with crushed nuts.

senses.meaning: marked with scars
senses.here: Her scarred hands — her hands marked with old scars.
senses.example: Her scarred hands clung to him.

seasons.meaning: the four parts of the year: spring, summer, autumn, winter

senses.meaning: the four parts of the year: spring, summer, autumn, winter
senses.here: the changing of the seasons — how spring, summer, autumn and winter change.
senses.example: When the direwolf howled again, Tyrion shut the heavy leather-bound cover on the book he was reading, a hundred-year-old discourse on the changing of the seasons by a long-dead maester.

senses.meaning: shaking from cold or fear.
senses.here: Will sits shaking with cold on his horse.
senses.example: It is hard to take orders from a man you laughed at in your cups, Will reflected as he sat shivering atop his garron.

senses.meaning: sounding like a sigh
senses.here: A soft sighing sound: like a sigh, as if a million people breathed out.
senses.example: Dimly, as if from far away, she heard a… a noise… a soft sighing sound, as if a million people had let out their breath at once.

senses.meaning: a high shrill sound
senses.here: She hears the wind’s high cry.
senses.example: She listened to the skirling of the wind and the scuffling sound of leather on stone.

senses.meaning: killed (past of slay)
senses.here: Asks whether it is for the brother he killed.
senses.example: For the brother you slew, or the child you stole?

smoldering.meaning: burning slowly without flame; glowing like hot embers

senses.meaning: burning slowly without flame; glowing like hot embers
senses.here: Eyes of polished garnet smoldered in the black marble faces of the sphinxes.
senses.example: The walls were hung with tapestries from Norvos and Qohor and Lys, and a pair of Valyrian sphinxes flanked the door, eyes of polished garnet smoldering in black marble faces.

senses.meaning: at some time.
senses.here: He will be glad if she has washed even once this year.
senses.example: “If she has washed sometime this year, I shall be glad.

senses.meaning: lively
senses.here: It says the young female horse was lively and splendid.
senses.example: She was a young filly, spirited and splendid.

senses.meaning: directly; straight.
senses.here: The Starks sit squarely across the line of supply; directly across.
senses.example: Jaime’s host is all slaughtered or taken or put to flight, and the Starks and the Tullys sit squarely across our line of supply.

steaming.meaning: giving off steam; very hot and wet

senses.meaning: giving off steam; very hot and wet
senses.here: Catelyn’s bath was always hot and steaming.
senses.example: Catelyn’s bath was always hot and steaming, and her walls warm to the touch.

streaming.meaning: flowing out behind in the wind

senses.meaning: flowing out behind in the wind
senses.here: His cloak flows out behind him as he rides.
senses.example: The foot soldiers and townsfolk were cheering Robb as he rode past, Bran knew; cheering for Lord Stark, for the Lord of Winterfell on his great stallion, with his cloak streaming and Grey Wind racing beside him.

senses.meaning: solid; real.
senses.here: His fading body seems less solid and real than the wind.
senses.example: One moment he was there and the next he was fading, his flesh colorless, less substantial than the wind.

senses.meaning: the light of the sun.
senses.here: The rubies on his chest armor flash like fire in the sun's light.
senses.example: On his breastplate was the three-headed dragon of his House, wrought all in rubies that flashed like fire in the sunlight.

swelling.meaning: a part of the body grown big from hurt

senses.meaning: a part of the body grown big from hurt
senses.here: The swollen place has gone down.
senses.example: The angry plum color had faded to yellow, and the swelling was down, but there was no mistaking it for anything but what it was.

senses.meaning: higher; bigger in height
senses.here: The taller guard walks down the alley.
senses.example: The taller of the guardsmen started down the alley.

tenting.meaning: fabric roofing; the cloth of a tent

senses.meaning: fabric roofing; the cloth of a tent
senses.here: the silk cloth roof of Khal Drogo’s hall was rolled up so the moon shone in.
senses.example: The silk tenting that roofed Khal Drogo’s hall had been rolled up tonight, and the moon followed them inside.

senses.meaning: growing thinner; becoming less dense
senses.here: the underbrush thinning means the low bushes growing less thick
senses.example: Here was a hush in the night, moonlight and shadows, a thick carpet of dead leaves underfoot, densely wooded ridges sloping gently down to the streambed, the underbrush thinning as the ground fell away.

town.meaning: Wendish Town: a place whose people are dead

senses.meaning: Wendish Town: a place whose people are dead
senses.here: The people of Wendish Town are dead, like the rest.
senses.example: The rest are dead, along with the people of Wendish Town and the Mummer’s Ford.

senses.meaning: something that fools the eyes
senses.here: It says it may have been only a fooling sight of the moonlight.
senses.example: Perhaps it had only been a bird, a reflection on the snow, some trick of the moonlight.

senses.meaning: under; below.
senses.here: Will slides in under, flat on his belly.
senses.example: Will slid in underneath, flat on his belly in the snow and the mud, and looked down on the empty clearing below.

senses.meaning: not harmed or bothered
senses.here: The riders let the traders come and go unharmed, so long as they keep the peace of the holy city.
senses.example: The riders let them come and go unmolested, so long as they observed the peace of the sacred city, did not profane the Mother of Mountains or the Womb of the World, and honored the crones of the dosh khaleen with the traditional gifts of salt, silver, and seed.

senses.meaning: on a higher floor
senses.here: Your lady awaits you upstairs: on the floor above.
senses.example: “Your lady awaits you upstairs.”

senses.meaning: curved like an arch
senses.here: His laugh echoes off the curved stone ceiling.
senses.example: Robert laughed, the sound rattling among the tombs and bouncing from the vaulted ceiling.

senses.meaning: to grow weaker
senses.here: Bran seemed to weaken means the boy seemed to grow weaker and fade
senses.example: The maester said they closed the window once, to shut out the noise, and Bran seemed to weaken.

senses.meaning: shouting with joy
senses.here: A whooping gang — a gang of children shouting with joy.
senses.example: A whooping gang of small children went running past, chasing a rolling hoop.

senses.meaning: a young wolf.
senses.here: Arya hugs the young wolf tight.
senses.example: Arya made a face and hugged the wolfling tight.

wrap.meaning: to cover by folding cloth, furs, or paper around

senses.meaning: to cover by folding cloth, furs, or paper around
senses.here: Wrapped in his furs and leathers, his father loomed over him like a giant.
senses.example: Wrapped in his furs and leathers, mounted on his great warhorse, his lord father loomed over him like a giant.

zelazny.meaning: Roger Zelazny, an author Martin thanks in the acknowledgments

senses.meaning: Roger Zelazny, an author Martin thanks in the acknowledgments
senses.here: Roger Zelazny is named among the friends Martin thanks for help with details.
senses.example: so I could get all those little details right—to Sage Walker, Martin Wright, Melinda Snodgrass, Carl Keim, Bruce Baugh, Tim O’Brien, Roger Zelazny, Jane Lindskold, and Laura J. Mixon, and of course to Parris.

ride.here: Will wanted nothing so much as to ride hellbent for the safety of the Wall.

senses.meaning: to travel on a horse
senses.here: Will wanted nothing so much as to ride hellbent for the safety of the Wall.

senses.meaning: a journey on a horse
senses.here: We have a long ride before us. Eight days, maybe nine.

anchors.context: “We have a long ride before us,” Gared pointed out.

bottom.here: The bottom of the bowl was covered with tiny pink rocks.

senses.meaning: the lowest part of something
senses.here: They reached the bottom of the stairs.

take the black.meaning: To join the Night's Watch, the brotherhood that guards the Wall; its men all wear black.
take the black.here: Maester Luwin tells Ned that Jon wants to join the Night's Watch.
take the black.example: It seems the boy aspires to take the black.

put on the black.meaning: To join the Night's Watch; to become one of the black-clad brothers.
put on the black.here: Will the poacher was given a choice: join the Night's Watch or lose a hand.
put on the black.example: it had been a choice of putting on the black or losing a hand.

iron throne.meaning: The throne of the king of the Seven Kingdoms, made from the melted swords of defeated enemies.
iron throne.here: Robert, called the Usurper, sits on the Iron Throne while the Targaryen children beg in exile.
iron throne.example: as the years passed and the Usurper continued to sit upon the Iron Throne, doors closed and their lives grew meaner.

winter is coming.meaning: The words of House Stark: a warning to always be ready for hard times ahead.
winter is coming.here: Ned says it as a warning that hard times are always ahead.

milk of the poppy.meaning: A strong medicine made from poppies that takes away pain and makes people sleep.
milk of the poppy.here: Maester Pycelle gives it to the dying Jon Arryn so he will not suffer.
milk of the poppy.example: he brought the milk of the poppy, so Jon did not linger long in pain.

seven hells.meaning: A curse; a rude way to say hell when angry or shocked.
seven hells.here: Theon Greyjoy shouts it when he is shocked.
seven hells.example: What in the seven hells is it?

blood of the dragon.meaning: Targaryen blood; being a true Targaryen, descended from the dragonlords of old Valyria.
blood of the dragon.here: Dany tells herself she is a true Targaryen, strong like the dragons of old.
blood of the dragon.example: I am blood of the dragon, she told herself.

blood of my blood.meaning: A Dothraki way to say my sworn brother; one bound to you by oath, not by birth.
blood of my blood.here: Dany speaks to her husband Drogo's bloodriders, who are bound to him by oath.
blood of my blood.example: “This is a gift worthy of a great warrior, O blood of my blood, and I am but a woman.

hand of the king.meaning: The king's chief helper and second-in-command, who rules when the king will not.
hand of the king.here: Jon Arryn served as Hand; now Robert wants Ned Stark for the office.
hand of the king.example: He served as Lord of the Eyrie, as Warden of the East, as the Hand of the King.

master at arms.meaning: The officer in a castle who teaches fighting and trains the soldiers.
master at arms.here: Ser Rodrik Cassel is Winterfell's master-at-arms, drilling the boys with wooden swords.
master at arms.example: under the watchful eye of old Ser Rodrik Cassel, the master-at-arms, a great stout keg of a man with magnificent white cheek whiskers.

men at arms.meaning: Ordinary soldiers who serve a lord; fighting men, not knights.
men at arms.here: The kings' armies are counted in knights, freeriders, and men-at-arms.
men at arms.example: five thousand mounted knights, and ten times as many freeriders and men-at-arms.

king beyond the wall.meaning: The leader of the wildlings, the free people living north of the Wall.
king beyond the wall.here: Mance Rayder is the wildling leader the deserter served.
king beyond the wall.example: his sword sworn to Mance Rayder, the King-beyond-the-Wall.

dosh khaleen.meaning: The council of old widows of dead khals at Vaes Dothrak, whom every new khaleesi must visit.
dosh khaleen.here: Illyrio says Drogo must present Dany to the dosh khaleen after the wedding.
dosh khaleen.example: he must make his procession across the plains and present her to the dosh khaleen at Vaes Dothrak.

beggar king.meaning: A mocking name for Viserys Targaryen, the exiled prince who begs for help to win back his throne.
beggar king.here: People in Pentos mock Viserys as the beggar king; Robert fears he will return with a Dothraki army.
beggar king.example: In the alleys and wine sinks of Pentos, they called her brother “the beggar king.”

mad king.meaning: Aerys II Targaryen, the cruel insane king whom Robert overthrew.
mad king.here: Ned remembers how the Mad King demanded his and Robert's heads, starting the rebellion.
mad king.example: When the Mad King Aerys II Targaryen had demanded their heads, the Lord of the Eyrie had raised his moon-and-falcon banners in revolt rather than give up those he had pledged to protect.

master of whisperers.meaning: The spymaster on the king's small council, in charge of secrets and spies.
master of whisperers.here: Varys the eunuch holds this office on Robert's council.
master of whisperers.example: Varys the eunuch was the king’s master of whisperers.

dark wings dark words.meaning: A saying: bad news travels by raven; when ravens come, the news is usually bad.
dark wings dark words.here: Ned murmurs the old saying when a raven brings Lysa's letter.

call the banners.meaning: To summon the lords and their armies to war.
call the banners.here: Ned warns he may have to summon the northern armies against the wildling king.
call the banners.example: The day may come when I will have no choice but to call the banners and ride north to deal with this King-beyond-the-Wall for good and all.

cloth of gold.meaning: Costly cloth woven with gold thread.
cloth of gold.here: Renly wears a half cape of cloth-of-gold, showing off his wealth.
cloth of gold.example: A cloth-of-gold half cape was draped casually across one shoulder, fastened with an emerald brooch.

moon and falcon.meaning: The badge of House Arryn: a falcon and a moon.
moon and falcon.here: The Arryn banners and seal carry the moon-and-falcon.
moon and falcon.example: the Lord of the Eyrie had raised his moon-and-falcon banners in revolt rather than give up those he had pledged to protect.

half dozen.here: Benjen Stark will lead six men ranging into the haunted forest.
half dozen.example: Benjen Stark was to lead a half-dozen men on a ranging into the haunted forest.

small council.meaning: The king's council of chief officers who help rule the Seven Kingdoms.
small council.here: Pycelle calls an urgent meeting of the small council in the Red Keep.
small council.example: Grand Maester Pycelle had convened an urgent meeting of the small council.

master of coin.meaning: The officer in charge of the kingdom's money and treasury.
master of coin.here: Littlefinger, Petyr Baelish, holds this office on the small council.
master of coin.example: I am master of coin, the king’s own councillor.

grand maester.meaning: The chief maester, a learned man who serves the king as healer and adviser.
grand maester.here: Grand Maester Pycelle serves on Robert's small council.
grand maester.example: This morning he commanded me to ride ahead with all haste and ask Grand Maester Pycelle to convene this council at once.

lord commander.meaning: The leader of the Kingsguard, or of the Night's Watch.
lord commander.here: Ser Barristan Selmy leads the Kingsguard.
lord commander.example: The greatest living knight was Ser Barristan Selmy, Barristan the Bold, the Lord Commander of the Kingsguard.

high septon.meaning: The head of the Faith, the chief priest of the Seven.
high septon.here: Catelyn was anointed by the High Septon himself when she was a girl.
high septon.example: “Anointed with the seven oils by the High Septon himself.”

the seven.meaning: The seven gods worshipped in the south: Father, Mother, Warrior, Maiden, Smith, Crone, and Stranger.
the seven.here: Catelyn follows the Faith; Ned built her a sept so she can sing to the seven faces of god.
the seven.example: For her sake, Ned had built a small sept where she might sing to the seven faces of god, but the blood of the First Men still flowed in the veins of the Starks, and his own gods were the old ones, the nameless, faceless gods of the greenwood they shared with the vanished children of the forest.

heart tree.meaning: A white weirwood tree with a face carved in its bark, holy to the old gods.
heart tree.here: The heart tree in Winterfell's godswood has a face carved in its bark.

children of the forest.meaning: The small ancient people who lived in Westeros before men came.
children of the forest.here: Old Nan's tale tells of the last hero seeking the children and their magic in the Long Night.
children of the forest.example: the last hero determined to seek out the children, in the hopes that their ancient magics could win back what the armies of men had lost.

the others.meaning: The mysterious cold dead creatures beyond the Wall; the great enemy.
the others.here: The Others move without a sound in the prologue; all men fear them.

white walkers.meaning: Another name for the Others, the icy dead enemies beyond the Wall.
white walkers.here: Mormont reports that fisherfolk have seen white walkers on the shore.
white walkers.example: The fisherfolk near Eastwatch have glimpsed white walkers on the shore.

free cities.meaning: The nine rich independent cities across the narrow sea, like Pentos and Braavos.
free cities.here: Illyrio says the Free Cities pay the Dothraki to leave them alone.
free cities.example: The Free Cities were always generous with the horselords.

first men.meaning: The first humans who came to Westeros, thousands of years ago; the Starks descend from them.
first men.here: The Starks still carry the blood of the First Men.
first men.example: the blood of the First Men still flowed in the veins of the Starks

kings in the north.meaning: The ancient Stark kings who ruled the north before the Targaryens came.
kings in the north.here: Winterfell's name goes back to when the Starks were Kings in the North.
kings in the north.example: The name it bore was older still, a legacy from the age of heroes, when the Starks were Kings in the North.

dance of the dragons.meaning: A great Targaryen civil war long ago, when brother fought sister with dragons.
dance of the dragons.here: Ser Erryk and Ser Arryk killed each other in that war.
dance of the dragons.example: The twins Ser Erryk and Ser Arryk, who had died on one another’s swords hundreds of years ago, when brother fought sister in the war the singers called the Dance of the Dragons.

long night.meaning: The terrible ancient winter when the Others first came.
long night.here: Old Nan tells how the Others came in that darkness.
long night.example: “In that darkness, the Others came for the first time,” she said

age of heroes.meaning: The ancient time of legends, when heroes like Brandon the Builder lived.
age of heroes.here: Ned's father told tales of the age of heroes and the children of the forest.
age of heroes.example: He had a grim cast to his grey eyes this day, and he seemed not at all the man who would sit before the fire in the evening and talk softly of the age of heroes and the children of the forest.

wake the dragon.meaning: To make Viserys, the last dragon, angry; to stir his cruel pride.
wake the dragon.here: Viserys warns Illyrio not to cheat him, or he will wake the dragon.
wake the dragon.example: “And if he tries to cheat me, he will learn to his sorrow what it means to wake the dragon,” Viserys had vowed, laying a hand on his borrowed sword.

it is known.meaning: A Dothraki saying: everyone knows it; it is certain.
it is known.here: The Dothraki girls say it as if it settles everything: the moon is a goddess.
it is known.example: Moon is no egg. Moon is god, woman wife of sun. It is known.

lord of light.meaning: The red god worshipped in the Free Cities, served by red priests.
lord of light.here: Illyrio greets Dany in the Lord of Light's name at her wedding.
lord of light.example: “May the Lord of Light shower you with blessings on this most fortunate day, Princess Daenerys,” the magister said as he took her hand.

demon of the trident.meaning: Robert Baratheon's battle nickname, from his great victory at the Trident.
demon of the trident.here: Jon remembers his father praising Robert as the peerless warrior, demon of the Trident.
demon of the trident.example: His father had talked of him often: the peerless Robert Baratheon, demon of the Trident, the fiercest warrior of the realm, a giant among princes.

dance with ilyn payne.meaning: To be executed; Ilyn Payne is the king's headsman.
dance with ilyn payne.here: Littlefinger warns Ned: accuse the king and you will be beheaded.
dance with ilyn payne.example: Accuse the king and you will dance with Ilyn Payne before the words are out of your mouth.

lord snow.meaning: A mocking title for Jon Snow, reminding him he is a bastard, not a true lord.
lord snow.here: Ser Alliser sneers Lord Snow at Jon in the training yard.

the spider.meaning: Varys's nickname; like a spider, he sits at the center of a web of spies.
the spider.here: Pycelle warns Ned not to trust spiders, meaning Varys.
the spider.example: Put not your trust in spiders, my lord.

old bear.meaning: The men's nickname for Lord Commander Jeor Mormont of the Night's Watch.
old bear.here: Tyrion warns the winch men that the Old Bear would punish them.
old bear.example: The Old Bear would have our hides.

knight of the gate.meaning: The commander who guards the Bloody Gate, the entrance to the Vale.
knight of the gate.here: Jon Arryn gave this office to Catelyn's uncle in the Vale.
knight of the gate.example: “Your uncle waits in the Vale, does he not? Jon named him Knight of the Gate, I’d heard.”

lord steward.meaning: The Night's Watch officer in charge of supplies and the daily running of Castle Black.
lord steward.here: Bowen Marsh, the Lord Steward, objects to Thorne's cruel nicknames.
lord steward.example: “Not so,” objected the Lord Steward, Bowen Marsh, a man as round and red as a pomegranate.

first ranger.meaning: The Night's Watch officer who leads the rangers on patrols beyond the Wall.
first ranger.here: Benjen Stark is First Ranger; he spends his days with the Lord Commander.
first ranger.example: He was First Ranger, and he spent his days and nights with Lord Commander Mormont and Maester Aemon and the other high officers, while Jon was given over to the less than tender charge of Ser Alliser Thorne.

sworn sword.meaning: A knight or fighting man sworn to serve a particular lord.
sworn sword.here: The king's party to Winterfell includes hundreds of knights and sworn swords.
sworn sword.example: The visitors poured through the castle gates in a river of gold and silver and polished steel, three hundred strong, a pride of bannermen and knights, of sworn swords and freeriders.

city watch.meaning: The guards of King's Landing, called gold cloaks for their golden cloaks.
city watch.here: Men of the City Watch come to take Catelyn to the castle.
city watch.example: The men who pushed into the room wore the black ringmail and golden cloaks of the City Watch.

white cloaks.meaning: The Kingsguard; the king's seven bodyguards, who wear white cloaks.
white cloaks.here: Two Kingsguard knights in white cloaks ride beside the king.
white cloaks.example: Yet the huge man at the head of the column, flanked by two knights in the snow-white cloaks of the Kingsguard, seemed almost a stranger to Ned

dancing master.meaning: Syrio Forel's cover title; he is really a master swordsman teaching Arya.
dancing master.here: Syrio tells Arya he is her dancing master as he hands her a wooden sword.

first sword of braavos.meaning: The finest swordsman of Braavos, champion of the Sealord.
first sword of braavos.here: Syrio says he was First Sword to the Sealord of Braavos for nine years.
first sword of braavos.example: Nine years Syrio Forel was first sword to the Sealord of Braavos, he knows these things.
forms: first sword to the sealord of braavos

water dance.meaning: The swift Braavosi sword-fighting style that Syrio teaches Arya.
water dance.here: Syrio contrasts it with the heavy iron dance of Westerosi knights.
water dance.example: This is the bravo’s dance, the water dance, swift and sudden.

the pointy end.meaning: The sharp tip of a sword; the part to stab with.
the pointy end.here: Jon's first sword lesson to Arya: stab with the point.
forms: stick them with the pointy end

tower of the hand.meaning: The tower in the Red Keep where the Hand of the King lives and works.
tower of the hand.here: Ned is given Jon Arryn's old rooms in the Tower of the Hand.
tower of the hand.example: “Yes, my lord,” the steward said. “We have given you Lord Arryn’s former chambers in the Tower of the Hand, if it please you.

coat of arms.meaning: The special picture or badge of a noble house, worn on shields and clothes.
coat of arms.here: Arya jokes that a girl who cannot fight needs no coat of arms.
coat of arms.example: “That would look silly. Besides, if a girl can’t fight, why should she have a coat of arms?”

iron bank.meaning: The rich and powerful bank of Braavos that lends money even to kings.
iron bank.here: The crown owes huge debts, partly to the Iron Bank of Braavos.
iron bank.example: “The Crown is more than six million gold pieces in debt, Lord Stark. The Lannisters are the biggest part of it, but we have also borrowed from Lord Tyrell, the Iron Bank of Braavos, and several Tyroshi trading cartels.

valyrian steel.meaning: Rare magic steel from old Valyria; nothing holds an edge like it.
valyrian steel.here: Ned's greatsword Ice is Valyrian steel, dark as smoke.
valyrian steel.example: The blade was Valyrian steel, spell-forged and dark as smoke.

mail and plate.meaning: Armor made of chain links (mail) and steel plates (plate).
mail and plate.here: The fat new recruit brings his own armor: mail and plate and helm.
mail and plate.example: It was soon revealed that the new recruit had brought his own armor with him; padded doublet, boiled leather, mail and plate and helm, even a great wood-and-leather shield blazoned with the same striding huntsman he wore on his surcoat.

boiled leather.meaning: Leather hardened by boiling, used as light armor.
boiled leather.here: Waymar Royce wears boiled leather under his ringmail.
boiled leather.example: a fine supple coat of gleaming black ringmail over layers of black wool and boiled leather.

live steel.meaning: Real sharp swords, as opposed to blunted practice swords.
live steel.here: The master-at-arms forbids live steel for the boys' practice.
live steel.example: “Live steel is too dangerous. I will permit you tourney swords, with blunted edges.”

beyond the wall.meaning: The wild lands north of the Wall, home to wildlings and worse.
beyond the wall.here: Old Nan warns of darker things beyond the Wall.
beyond the wall.example: “There are darker things beyond the Wall.”

grumkins and snarks.meaning: Monsters from Old Nan's scary stories for children.
grumkins and snarks.here: Tyrion teases Jon that the Watch only guards against storybook monsters.
grumkins and snarks.example: Sullen peasants, debtors, poachers, rapers, thieves, and bastards like you all wind up on the Wall, watching for grumkins and snarks and all the other monsters your wet nurse warned you about.

green men.meaning: The mysterious guardians of the Isle of Faces, who keep silent watch.
green men.here: Only on the Isle of Faces do the green men still guard the last southern weirwoods.
green men.example: In the south the last weirwoods had been cut down or burned out a thousand years ago, except on the Isle of Faces where the green men kept their silent watch.

name day.meaning: A birthday; the anniversary of the day one was named.
name day.here: Robert gave a tourney for his son's name day, when Jon Arryn still seemed healthy.
name day.example: We gave a tourney on my son’s name day.

babe in arms.meaning: A tiny baby, too young to walk; carried in arms.
babe in arms.here: Rhaegar's baby son was torn from his mother and killed.
babe in arms.example: The boy had been no more than a babe in arms, yet Lord Tywin’s soldiers had torn him from his mother’s breast and dashed his head against a wall.

give suck.here: Robb offers to feed the motherless direwolf pup with warm milk.
give suck.example: I will soak a towel with warm milk, and give him suck from that.

wet nurse.meaning: A woman paid to breastfeed another woman's baby.
wet nurse.here: Royce jokes that even his wet nurse warned him about the cold.
wet nurse.example: “My wet nurse said the same thing, Will,” Royce replied.

blood right.meaning: The right to rule because of one's birth and bloodline.
blood right.here: Viserys claims Westeros is his by blood right, stolen by treachery.
blood right.example: “Ours by blood right, taken from us by treachery, but ours still, ours forever.

liege lord.meaning: The lord to whom one owes loyalty and service.
liege lord.here: Robert says Jon Arryn's service was the duty owed his liege lord.
liege lord.example: Jon’s service was the duty he owed his liege lord.

pledge fealty.meaning: To swear loyalty and service to a lord or king.
pledge fealty.here: King Loren surrendered and pledged his fealty to the Targaryens.
pledge fealty.example: King Loren had escaped, and lived long enough to surrender, pledge his fealty to the Targaryens, and beget a son, for which Tyrion was duly grateful.

wolf blood.meaning: The wild fierce Stark temper; Ned says Arya has it like Lyanna did.
wolf blood.here: Ned tells Arya her wildness is the wolf blood of the Starks.
wolf blood.example: ‘The wolf blood,’ my father used to call it.

game of thrones.meaning: The dangerous struggle among great houses for power over the kingdom.
game of thrones.here: Jorah says the high lords play their game of thrones while the common people suffer.
game of thrones.example: “The common people pray for rain, healthy children, and a summer that never ends,” Ser Jorah told her. “It is no matter to them if the high lords play their game of thrones, so long as they are left in peace.”

the seed is strong.meaning: Jon Arryn's dying words: the children strongly take after their true father. Seed means children.
the seed is strong.here: Pycelle reports Jon Arryn's last whisper about Robert's seed, his children.
the seed is strong.example: The seed is strong, he said.

little birds.meaning: Varys's spies and informers, who whisper secrets to him.
little birds.here: Littlefinger warns Ned that one of Varys's little birds heard of Catelyn's visit.
little birds.example: His little birds, he calls them. One of his little birds heard about your visit.

common tongue.meaning: The shared language of the Seven Kingdoms, spoken from Winterfell to Dorne.
common tongue.here: The khal knows only a few words of bastard Valyrian and none of the Common Tongue.
common tongue.example: Dothraki was incomprehensible to her, and the khal knew only a few words of the bastard Valyrian of the Free Cities, and none at all of the Common Tongue of the Seven Kingdoms.

far eyes.meaning: Lookouts; scouts who watch from far away, also the lookouts on a ship.
far eyes.here: Will spots a wildling woman acting as a lookout in the trees.
far eyes.example: There’s one woman up an ironwood, half-hid in the branches. A far-eyes.

pitch dark.meaning: Completely dark; black as pitch, which is tar.
pitch dark.here: The streets of Pentos are pitch-dark when Dany sets out.
pitch dark.example: The streets of Pentos were pitch-dark when they set out in Illyrio’s elaborately carved palanquin.

red handed.meaning: Caught while doing something wrong, with the proof still in hand.
red handed.here: Will the poacher was caught skinning the Mallisters' deer.
red handed.example: Mallister freeriders had caught him red-handed in the Mallisters’ own woods, skinning one of the Mallisters’ own bucks, and it had been a choice of putting on the black or losing a hand.

hard pressed.meaning: Having difficulty; struggling to keep up.
hard pressed.here: Sansa can barely keep up with Joffrey's fast riding.
hard pressed.example: Sansa was hard-pressed to keep up on her mare.

the rookery.meaning: The tower room where the messenger ravens are kept.
the rookery.here: Bran knows Winterfell's secrets, including the way to the rookery.
the rookery.example: There was a covered bridge that went from the fourth floor of the bell tower across to the second floor of the rookery.

black brothers.meaning: The men of the Night's Watch, who all wear black.
black brothers.here: Yoren the wandering crow joins the party as one of the black brothers.
black brothers.example: they stayed a night behind the wooden walls of a forest holdfast, and there joined up with another of the black brothers, one Yoren.

forge your chain.meaning: To study to become a maester; each link of the chain is earned by learning.
forge your chain.here: Pycelle remembers his youth at the Citadel, still studying to be a maester.
forge your chain.example: I was a young man then, still forging my chain.

dark art.here: Robert swears Varys learns secrets by some dark magic.
dark art.example: But Varys has ways of learning things that no man could know. He has some dark art, Ned, I swear it.

rise to the bait.meaning: To react to a tease or provocation; to take the tease seriously.
rise to the bait.here: Royce teases the old ranger Gared, but Gared will not be drawn in.
rise to the bait.example: Gared did not rise to the bait.

make light of.meaning: To treat something as unimportant; to joke about it.
make light of.here: Gared is angry because Royce joked about his fears.
make light of.example: Gared had spent forty years in the Night’s Watch, man and boy, and he was not accustomed to being made light of.

brook no argument.meaning: To allow no disagreement; to refuse to discuss it.
brook no argument.here: Ned speaks firmly: Robb must rule the north in his place.
brook no argument.example: “Yes,” Ned said, in words that would brook no argument.

old hand at.meaning: Experienced at; skilled from long practice.
old hand at.here: Jon, only fourteen, has watched many executions with his father.
old hand at.example: Jon was fourteen, an old hand at justice.

by fits and starts.meaning: Stopping and starting; not steady or smooth.
by fits and starts.here: Tyrion climbs the Wall in the winch cage, jerking upward unevenly.
by fits and starts.example: He moved upward slowly, by fits and starts at first, then more smoothly.

at a loss.meaning: Confused; not knowing what to do or say.
at a loss.here: For once even Tyrion does not know what to say to Maester Aemon.
at a loss.example: For once, Tyrion Lannister found himself at a loss for words.

have a mind to.meaning: To intend to; to want to.
have a mind to.here: Tyrion decides he wants to see the Wall with his own eyes.
have a mind to.example: I have a mind to go with them and see this Wall we have all heard so much of.

count on.meaning: To rely on; to trust that something will happen.
count on.here: Ned tells Littlefinger he will not melt away; Littlefinger can rely on that.
count on.example: “I do not plan on melting soon, Lord Baelish. You may count on it.”

give the lie.meaning: To call someone a liar; to show their words are false.
give the lie.here: Littlefinger says no one is left alive to call Tyrion a liar about the dagger.
give the lie.example: “A sweet piece of steel, but it cuts two ways, my lord. The Imp will no doubt swear the blade was lost or stolen while he was at Winterfell, and with his hireling dead, who is there to give him the lie?”

bide your time.meaning: To wait patiently for the right moment to act.
bide your time.here: Robert fears the Targaryen loyalists are quietly waiting to strike.
bide your time.example: They bide their time for now, but give them half a chance, they will murder me in my bed, and my sons with me.

in your cups.meaning: Drunk; having drunk too much wine.
in your cups.here: Jon sees the fat king walking unsteadily, clearly drunk.
in your cups.example: He walked like a man half in his cups.

cut down.meaning: To cut someone loose from where they hang or are tied.
cut down.here: Ned has the bound deserter cut loose from the holdfast wall.
cut down.example: The breath of man and horse mingled, steaming, in the cold morning air as his lord father had the man cut down from the wall and dragged before them.

call a halt.meaning: To stop something for now, especially a meeting.
call a halt.here: Ned ends the small council meeting; they will continue tomorrow.
call a halt.example: Let us call a halt for today and resume when we are fresher.

make common cause.meaning: To join forces with someone, even one you dislike, for a shared purpose.
make common cause.here: Ned forces himself to work with the despised Littlefinger.
make common cause.example: It would not be the first time that Ned had been forced to make common cause with a man he despised.

fall to your knees.meaning: To kneel down, to beg or to show deep respect.
fall to your knees.here: Tyrion tells Joffrey to kneel before the Starks and beg forgiveness.
fall to your knees.example: But first you get yourself to Lord and Lady Stark, and you fall to your knees in front of them, and you tell them how very sorry you are, and that you are at their service if there is the slightest thing you can do for them or theirs in this desperate hour, and that all your prayers go with them.

draw blood.meaning: To break the skin so that blood comes out.
draw blood.here: Ghost nips Rast's throat just enough to frighten him.
draw blood.example: his teeth nipped lightly at the soft skin of the boy’s throat, just enough to draw blood.

crack a smile.meaning: To smile just a little, often unwillingly.
crack a smile.here: Only sour Ser Alliser will not even smile at the feast.
crack a smile.example: Ser Alliser Thorne was the only man at table who did not so much as crack a smile.

clean your plate.meaning: To eat all the food on your plate.
clean your plate.here: Septa Mordane scolds Arya for not eating.
clean your plate.example: You will sit down and clean your plate.

at your heels.here: Arya runs to the yard with her wolf Nymeria close behind.
at your heels.example: She got up and ran, the wolf coming hard at her heels.

in a heartbeat.here: Sam's sobs turn to laughter the moment Ghost licks his face.
in a heartbeat.example: It was Ghost who knew what to do. Silent as shadow, the pale direwolf moved closer and began to lick the warm tears off Samwell Tarly’s face. The fat boy cried out, startled… and somehow, in a heartbeat, his sobs turned to laughter.

for good and all.here: Ned may have to march north to settle the wildling king permanently.
for good and all.example: The day may come when I will have no choice but to call the banners and ride north to deal with this King-beyond-the-Wall for good and all.

by the score.meaning: In large numbers; a score is twenty.
by the score.here: Old Nan tells how the Others killed heroes and armies by the dozen.
by the score.example: They swept over holdfasts and cities and kingdoms, felled heroes and armies by the score, riding their pale dead horses and leading hosts of the slain.

close on.here: Catelyn has sat by Bran's bed for almost two weeks.
close on.example: She had been there, day and night, for close on a fortnight.

a shade more.here: Jon teases that riding is only slightly more tiring than needlework.
a shade more.example: “A shade more exhausting than needlework,” Jon observed.

as good as his word.meaning: Keeping one's promises; doing what one said.
as good as his word.here: Tyrion promises Mormont he will speak to the king, and he means it.
as good as his word.example: Tyrion Lannister was as good as his word.

be that as it may.meaning: Even so; however that may be.
be that as it may.example: “The wiser answer was no, my lord, but be that as it may.

for all the world.here: Tyrion perched above the door looks just like a gargoyle.
for all the world.example: Tyrion Lannister was sitting on the ledge above the door to the Great Hall, looking for all the world like a gargoyle.

to a fault.meaning: Too much; more than is good.
to a fault.here: Ser Rodrik is stubborn and loyal, too loyal, Catelyn thinks.
to a fault.example: Old he might be, but he was stubborn, and loyal to a fault.

would that.meaning: I wish that; an old way to say if only.
would that.here: Catelyn wishes she could refuse the king's summons.

in earnest.here: Viserys has never really used a sword in a true fight.
in earnest.example: Dany knew he had never used a sword in earnest.

deadly earnest.meaning: Completely serious; not joking at all.
deadly earnest.here: Tyrion realizes old Mormont truly believes the Watch needs help.
deadly earnest.example: He was in deadly earnest, Tyrion realized.

all haste.meaning: As fast as possible; with great speed.
all haste.here: The king orders Renly to ride ahead at full speed to call the council.
all haste.example: This morning he commanded me to ride ahead with all haste and ask Grand Maester Pycelle to convene this council at once.

in your stead.meaning: In your place; instead of you.
in your stead.here: Ned tells Robb to rule Winterfell while he is away.
in your stead.example: You must govern the north in my stead, while I run Robert’s errands.

by your leave.meaning: With your permission; a formal polite goodbye.
by your leave.here: Arya bows stiffly to Myrcella before running off.

if it please you.meaning: If you like; if you agree. A formal polite phrase.
if it please you.here: The Hound offers to kill Lady, if Sansa wishes it.
if it please you.example: “I could silence the creature, if it please you,”

far be it from me.meaning: I would not dare or presume to do something.
far be it from me.here: Littlefinger will not try to talk Ned out of his dangerous plan.
far be it from me.example: If you are so eager to molder beside him, far be it from me to dissuade you, but I would rather not be included in the party, thank you very much.

beneath contempt.meaning: Too low and shameful to deserve respect or notice.
beneath contempt.here: Pycelle says even a poisoner is beneath contempt.
beneath contempt.example: Grand Maester Aethelmure wrote that all men carry murder in their hearts, yet even so, the poisoner is beneath contempt.

play the fool.meaning: To act like a fool; to do something stupid.
play the fool.here: Cersei warns Jaime not to be stupid about Ned Stark.

a head for figures.meaning: A talent for numbers and counting.
a head for figures.here: Arya notes Sansa was never good with numbers or household accounts.
a head for figures.example: Sansa had never had much of a head for figures.

have a care.here: Joffrey warns Sansa to watch how she speaks to his betrothed.
have a care.example: “Have a care how you address my betrothed.”

have your hides.here: The winch men warn Tyrion the Old Bear would punish them.
have your hides.example: The Old Bear would have our hides.

hemmed in.meaning: Surrounded; shut in with no way out.
hemmed in.here: Dany's horse is trapped between firepits with no room to stop.
hemmed in.example: They were hemmed in on either side, with no room to stop.

at bay.meaning: Kept away; held off at a distance.
at bay.here: The black brothers cut back the forest so no enemy can approach unseen.
at bay.example: Castle Black had a prodigious appetite for firewood, and here the forest was still kept at bay by the axes of the black brothers.

dead of night.meaning: The middle of the night; the darkest hours.
dead of night.here: Old Nan's tales say the wildlings steal children in the darkest night.
dead of night.example: They consorted with giants and ghouls, stole girl children in the dead of night, and drank blood from polished horns.

at first light.meaning: At dawn; as soon as the sun rises.
at first light.here: Tyrion must rise at dawn to ride with Yoren.
at first light.example: Yoren is determined to ride at first light.

in the blink of an eye.meaning: In an instant; faster than you can blink.
in the blink of an eye.here: At Dany's wedding feast, a quarrel turns into a swordfight in seconds.
in the blink of an eye.example: She heard a shout, saw a shove, and in the blink of an eye the arakhs were out, long razor-sharp blades, half sword and half scythe.

chill to the bone.meaning: To be frozen through; chilled completely.
chill to the bone.here: Tyrion is frozen after a week of hard riding in the cold.
chill to the bone.example: By the end of the first week, Tyrion’s thighs were raw from hard riding, his legs were cramping badly, and he was chilled to the bone.

change your mind.meaning: To decide differently; to change one's decision.
change your mind.here: Catelyn prayed Ned would decide to leave Bran at Winterfell.
change your mind.example: “I prayed for it,” she said dully. “He was my special boy. I went to the sept and prayed seven times to the seven faces of god that Ned would change his mind and leave him here with me.

take your leave.meaning: To say goodbye and go; to depart formally.
take your leave.here: Sam says goodbye to Jon and leaves.
take your leave.example: And so they were, he thought to himself after Sam had taken his leave.

pay your respects.meaning: To show honor, especially to the dead; to visit and honor.
pay your respects.here: Robert wants to visit the Stark tombs in the crypt.
pay your respects.example: “Take me down to your crypt, Eddard. I would pay my respects.”

see through.meaning: To not be fooled by; to see the truth behind.
see through.here: Even at fourteen, Jon sees Cersei's smile is false.
see through.example: Even at fourteen, Jon could see through her smile.

set forth.meaning: To begin a journey; to start out.
set forth.here: Bran's party rides out at dawn to see the deserter executed.
set forth.example: They set forth at daybreak to see a man beheaded, twenty in all, and Bran rode among them, nervous with excitement.

too clever by half.meaning: Too smart for one's own good; scheming and not to be trusted.
too clever by half.here: Ned does not trust the scheming Littlefinger.
too clever by half.example: That took Ned aback. Promise or no promise, he could not find it in him to trust Lord Petyr Baelish, who struck him as too clever by half.

out of patience.meaning: No longer willing to wait; annoyed and tired of waiting.
out of patience.here: Sansa is tired of waiting for Arya to obey.
out of patience.example: Sansa was running out of patience now.

hold your tongue.meaning: To keep silent; to stop talking.
hold your tongue.here: Robert orders Joffrey to stay silent until Arya finishes.
hold your tongue.example: “When she is done, you will have your turn. Until then, hold your tongue.”

break fast.meaning: To eat the first meal of the day; breakfast.
break fast.here: Tyrion goes off to eat his morning meal.

man and boy.here: Gared has served in the Night's Watch since he was a boy.
man and boy.example: Gared had spent forty years in the Night’s Watch, man and boy, and he was not accustomed to being made light of.

man grown.meaning: A grown man; an adult male. Old word order.
man grown.here: Jon insists he is nearly an adult.
man grown.example: “I am almost a man grown,” Jon protested.

green boy.meaning: A young inexperienced boy; green means new and untested.
green boy.here: Benjen tells Jon he is no ranger yet, only an untried boy.
green boy.example: You’re no ranger, Jon, only a green boy with the smell of summer still on you.

beggar the realm.meaning: To make the kingdom poor; to spend all its money.
beggar the realm.here: Ned refuses to believe Jon Arryn let Robert empty the treasury.
beggar the realm.example: “I will not believe that Jon Arryn allowed Robert to beggar the realm,” Ned said hotly.

dead meat.meaning: Certain to be killed or to fail; doomed.
dead meat.here: Noye tells Jon his beaten training partners would be dead in a real fight.
dead meat.example: “Four that you’ve humiliated in the yard. Four who are probably afraid of you. I’ve watched you fight. It’s not training with you. Put a good edge on your sword, and they’d be dead meat; you know it, I know it, they know it.

on a spike.meaning: A cut-off head stuck on a sharp post, displayed as a warning.
on a spike.here: Robert jokes he will put Ned's head on a spike if he says Your Grace again.
on a spike.example: “And if I hear ‘Your Grace’ once more, I’ll have your head on a spike.

make for.meaning: To head toward; to go in the direction of.
make for.here: Ned stands and heads for the door, ending the council meeting.
make for.example: He did not ask for their consent, but stood abruptly, nodded at them all, and made for the door.

put aside.here: Benjen tells Jon the Watch gives up their old families when they swear vows.
put aside.example: We put aside our old families when we swear our vows.

see to.meaning: To take care of; to deal with.
see to.here: Gared says he will take care of making the fire.
see to.example: “We need a fire. I’ll see to it.”

take chances.here: Illyrio says the Free Cities buy the Dothraki's friendship rather than risk war.
take chances.example: “The Lord of Light would hold our city walls against a million Dothraki, or so the red priests promise… yet why take chances, when their friendship comes so cheap?”

in the hopes that.meaning: Hoping that; with the hope that.
in the hopes that.here: The last hero sought the children of the forest, hoping their magic could save the world.
in the hopes that.example: the last hero determined to seek out the children, in the hopes that their ancient magics could win back what the armies of men had lost.

beg audience.meaning: To formally ask to meet and speak with someone important.
beg audience.here: Littlefinger asks to see Ned in his chambers.
beg audience.example: “My lord,” he said, “Lord Baelish is without and begs audience.”

look to.meaning: To turn to someone for help or guidance.
look to.here: Bran looks to his father to save him from the executioner's lesson.
look to.example: Bran looked to his lord father for rescue, but got only a frown, a furrowed brow.

take aback.here: Ned is shocked by Littlefinger's bold talk.

to your sorrow.meaning: So that you suffer for it; you will regret it.
to your sorrow.here: Ned warns Catelyn the Lannisters are merciless, as Aerys learned painfully.
to your sorrow.example: “The Lannisters are merciless in the face of weakness, as Aerys Targaryen learned to his sorrow, but they would not dare attack the north without all the power of the realm behind them, and that they shall not have.

peas in a pod.meaning: Very alike; like two peas in one pod.
peas in a pod.here: Tommen notes that Jaime and Tyrion are not much alike.
peas in a pod.example: Not like his brother, but then Jaime and Tyrion were somewhat less than peas in a pod themselves.

lie at your door.meaning: To be someone's fault or responsibility.
lie at your door.here: Ned tells Sansa the butcher's boy's death is the Hound's fault.
lie at your door.example: That murder lies at the Hound’s door, him and the cruel woman he serves.

sleep on it.meaning: To think about something overnight before deciding.
sleep on it.here: Robert tells Ned to take his time deciding about becoming Hand.
sleep on it.example: “Yes, yes, of course, tell Catelyn, sleep on it if you must.”

the likes of.here: Jeren sneers that Sam thinks himself too good for common boys.
the likes of.example: “The Lord of Ham thinks he’s too good to eat with the likes of us,” suggested Jeren.

the stone has been set.meaning: It is decided and cannot be changed.
the stone has been set.here: Robert refuses to discuss Jaime succeeding Tywin.
the stone has been set.example: Don’t vex me about this, Ned, the stone has been set.

make your flesh crawl.meaning: To give you a creepy feeling of fear or disgust.
make your flesh crawl.example: That was scarcely anything Ned needed to be told; there was something about Varys that made his flesh crawl.

take leave of your senses.meaning: To go mad; to lose one's reason.
take leave of your senses.here: Tyrion thinks his father would call him mad for asking about the Wall.
take leave of your senses.example: I will speak to my father and my brother Jaime as well.” And he would. Tyrion Lannister was as good as his word. He left the rest unsaid; that King Robert would ignore him, Lord Tywin would ask if he had taken leave of his senses, and Jaime would only laugh.

right hand.meaning: One's chief helper; most trusted supporter.
right hand.here: Ned sits beside the empty throne as Robert's Hand.
right hand.example: Ned took the chair beside it, as the right hand of his king.

have no business.meaning: To have no reason to deal with something; to keep away from it.
have no business.here: Gared says the living should not meddle with the dead.
have no business.example: “Dead is dead,” he said. “We have no business with the dead.”

the iron throne.meaning: the seat of the king of the Seven Kingdoms; the rule of the whole realm
the iron throne.here: The chair of swords in King's Landing. To sit it means to rule Westeros, and everyone fights over it.
the iron throne.example: Let them make their case before the Iron Throne and the lords of the land.

the hand of the king.meaning: the king's chief helper, who rules in his name when he is away
the hand of the king.here: Ned Stark holds this office. When Robert goes hunting, Ned sits the throne and speaks with the king's voice.
the hand of the king.example: “He slew the Hand of the King!”

the kingsguard.meaning: the king's bodyguards, knights in white cloaks who protect him for life
the kingsguard.here: The white-cloaked knights like Ser Barristan and Jaime Lannister who guard the king day and night.
the kingsguard.example: Between them stood fierce old Ser Gerold Hightower, the White Bull, Lord Commander of the Kingsguard.

the kingslayer.meaning: Jaime Lannister's hateful nickname, because he killed a king
the kingslayer.here: Men call Jaime this because he stabbed mad King Aerys in the back, breaking his sworn oath.
the kingslayer.example: “Your precious Kingslayer is hundreds of leagues from here,” snapped Lysa Arryn.

free folk.meaning: the wild people who live beyond the Wall and kneel to no king
free folk.here: Osha's people in the far north. They call themselves free because no lord rules them.
free folk.example: I was born up there, child, like my mother and her mother before her and her mother before her, born of the Free Folk.

the seven kingdoms.meaning: the whole realm of Westeros, seven lands under one king
the seven kingdoms.here: The land Robert rules from the Iron Throne, from the Wall to Dorne.
the seven kingdoms.example: Is the Eyrie not part of the Seven Kingdoms?

night watch.meaning: the order of men in black who guard the great Wall in the north
night watch.here: Jon's new order. Its men give up lands and wives, and deserting it means death.
night watch.example: and Father said he had been a deserter from the Night's Watch.

mother of mountains.meaning: the great holy mountain of the Dothraki, near their sacred city
mother of mountains.here: The mountain by Vaes Dothrak where the dosh khaleen live. Drogo climbs it to pray for a safe return.
mother of mountains.example: he must ascend the Mother of Mountains this night, to sacrifice to the gods for his safe return.

dothraki sea.meaning: the great grass plain where the Dothraki ride; they call grass a sea
dothraki sea.here: The endless grassland the khalasar crosses. To horse riders, the waving grass looks like water.
dothraki sea.example: “In Pentos, I make them with pork,” the old woman said, “but all my pigs died on the Dothraki sea.

battle axe.meaning: a heavy axe made for war
battle axe.here: The weapon Tyrion offers the mountain clansmen, and the axe on the Cerwyn shield.
battle axe.example: the battle-axe I carry would suit Shagga’s mighty hand far better

she wolf.here: Tyrion's angry name for Catelyn Stark, who has outwitted him and taken him prisoner.
she wolf.example: this seven-times-damned she-wolf Catelyn Stark had outwitted him at every turn.

standard bearer.meaning: the soldier who carries the lord's banner flag
standard bearer.here: The rider Catelyn's uncle sends ahead carrying the Tully double banner.
standard bearer.example: Her uncle sent a standard-bearer ahead of them, a double banner flying from his staff; the moon-and-falcon of House Arryn on high, and below it his own black fish.

hedge knight.meaning: a poor knight with no lord, who wanders looking for work
hedge knight.here: Knights like Ser Willis Wode, who own nothing but a horse and a sword and sell their fighting.
hedge knight.example: “We must have some rest, my lady,” the hedge knight Ser Willis Wode was saying to Catelyn Stark as Tyrion approached.

moon door.meaning: a door in the floor of the Eyrie that opens onto a deadly fall down the mountain
moon door.here: Lysa's way of killing people: they are thrown out of this door to fall hundreds of feet.
moon door.example: "Sister or no," she had replied, "if you try to steal my son, you will leave by the Moon Door."

the silent sisters.meaning: holy women of the Faith who prepare the dead for burial
the silent sisters.here: The quiet order that takes dead bodies and carries them north to Winterfell.
the silent sisters.example: "I gave them over to the silent sisters, to be sent north to Winterfell. Jory would want to lie beside his grandfather."

the lists.meaning: the fenced field where knights joust in a tourney
the lists.here: The tourney ground where warhorses charge at each other with lances.
the lists.example: The jousting went all day and into the dusk, the hooves of the great warhorses pounding down the lists until the field was a ragged wasteland of torn earth.

gold cloaks.meaning: the City Watch of King's Landing, who wear gold cloaks
gold cloaks.here: The city guards of the capital, commanded by Janos Slynt.
gold cloaks.example: “That’s the real king of this castle right there,” one of the gold cloaks had told her.

shadow lands.meaning: a far, strange land east of Asshai, at the edge of the known world
shadow lands.here: Where manticores and other strange things come from, beyond the eastern sea.
shadow lands.example: Those, Ser Jorah said, had likely come from the Shadow Lands beyond Asshai.

night lands.meaning: the Dothraki land of the dead
night lands.here: Where Dothraki believe dead warriors ride on. A khal's bloodriders die to follow him there.
night lands.example: his bloodriders died with him, to ride at his side in the night lands.

womb of the world.meaning: the great lake the Dothraki believe all life came from
womb of the world.here: The holy lake near Vaes Dothrak, ringed with reeds, where Dany rides.
womb of the world.example: They rode to the lake the Dothraki called the Womb of the World, surrounded by a fringe of reeds, its water still and calm.

stallion who mounts the world.meaning: the great leader the crones say will one day unite all Dothraki
stallion who mounts the world.here: The promised khal of khals. The dosh khaleen say Dany's unborn son is he.
stallion who mounts the world.example: “The prince is riding, and he shall be the stallion who mounts the world.”
forms: the stallion who mounts the world

faceless men.meaning: a secret group of killers from Braavos who can change their faces
faceless men.here: The feared assassins Pycelle names when the council talks of killing Daenerys.
faceless men.example: “On Braavos there is a society called the Faceless Men,” Grand Maester Pycelle offered.

master of horse.meaning: the servant in charge of a castle's horses and stables
master of horse.here: The office Robb gives to a young stableman while Hullen is away.
master of horse.example: a stick-thin stableman whom Robb had named master of horse while Hullen was away.

moon of my life.meaning: a Dothraki term of love for a wife, like “my darling”
moon of my life.here: What Drogo calls Dany. She is the moon that lights his life.
moon of my life.example: “Is good name, Dan Ares wife, moon of my life,” he said.

sun and stars.meaning: a Dothraki term of love for a husband, like “my darling”
sun and stars.example: "I pray that my sun-and-stars will not keep him waiting too long," she told Ser Jorah when her brother was out of earshot.

lizard lions.meaning: big dangerous reptiles that live in swamps, like crocodiles
lizard lions.here: The beasts in the Neck's black waters that guard the ruins of Moat Cailin.
lizard lions.example: cross a moat full of lizard-lions, and scale walls slimy with moss

two handed.here: A sword blow swung with both hands for full killing force.
two handed.example: Ser Gregor swung his sword, a savage two-handed blow that took the boy in the chest and knocked him from the saddle.

stone crows.meaning: one of the wild mountain clans of the Vale
stone crows.here: Gunthor son of Gurn's clan, who rob and kill travelers in the mountains.
stone crows.example: “When you meet your gods,” a different voice replied, “say it was Gunthor son of Gurn of the Stone Crows who sent you to them.”

as high as honor.meaning: the words of House Arryn: honor above everything
as high as honor.here: The Arryn motto. Tyrion throws it back at Lysa during his trial in the Eyrie.
as high as honor.example: “I presume that House Arryn remembers its own words,” the Imp said. “As High as Honor.”

the blood will tell.meaning: family blood always shows; a child will be like his kin
the blood will tell.here: Varys means Sansa will be like her mother Catelyn. Stark and Tully blood will show in her.

fear cuts deeper than swords.meaning: fear hurts and controls people more than weapons do
fear cuts deeper than swords.here: Syrio's lesson to Arya. Fear is the true enemy, sharper than any blade.
fear cuts deeper than swords.example: All halls lead somewhere. Where there is a way in, there is a way out. Fear cuts deeper than swords.

blood runs truer than oaths.meaning: family ties are stronger than promises
blood runs truer than oaths.here: Varys on Sansa's loyalty. Blood loyalty runs deeper than any sworn word.
blood runs truer than oaths.example: “Oh, so poignant,” said Varys. “And yet, it is truly said that blood runs truer than oaths.”

your grace.meaning: the respectful way to speak to a king or queen
your grace.here: How everyone must address Robert, Cersei, and Joffrey.
your grace.example: I told her to ask you to sup with me, if it pleases Your Grace.

wear the black.meaning: to be a member of the Night's Watch
wear the black.here: To wear the black cloak of the Watch. Two of the wildlings' prisoners are deserters.
wear the black.example: “Two of them wear the black,” he told Robb as he worked.

bend the knee.meaning: to kneel and swear loyalty; to give in to a ruler
bend the knee.here: To kneel before a lord or king and accept him as master.
bend the knee.example: when Robert next holds court, I’ll bend the knee and cry our need, see if the king and his Hand have some scum in the dungeons they’d be well rid of.

bend his neck.meaning: to bow to someone's rule; to submit
bend his neck.here: The Mountain will never submit to any man's justice.
bend his neck.example: The Mountain is not the sort to bend his neck to any man’s justice.

take his leave.here: To leave politely after a visit or meeting, as Ser Alliser does.
take his leave.example: And with that, Ser Alliser Thorne took his leave of them.

taken leave of your senses.here: Tyrion asks Catelyn if she has gone crazy, seizing him on the road.
taken leave of your senses.example: “Have you taken leave of your senses?”

taken aback.meaning: surprised and confused for a moment
taken aback.here: Jon did not expect what he just heard.

small wonder.here: Of course the clansmen left nine bodies behind; they were better fighters.
small wonder.example: Small wonder the clansmen had left nine bodies on the ground.

in their cups.here: The lords will laugh about Robb's mistake when they are drinking together.
in their cups.example: they will remember, and laugh about it in their cups.

care a fig.here: Jaime would not care in the least about a trial before being thrown off a mountain.
care a fig.example: "What will we gain by the dwarf's death? Do you imagine that Jaime will care a fig that we gave his brother a trial before we flung him off a mountain?"

bite the hand that feeds them.meaning: to harm the one who helps you
bite the hand that feeds them.here: Even hungry dogs do not turn on their masters, Littlefinger says dryly.
bite the hand that feeds them.example: "Even hungry dogs know better than to bite the hand that feeds them," Littlefinger called dryly.

food for crows.meaning: a dead body left for birds to eat
food for crows.here: A dead Tyrion would be worth nothing, just meat for the crows.
food for crows.example: Dead, he is only food for crows.

thick as thieves.meaning: very close friends who share secrets
thick as thieves.here: Bronn and Tyrion have become close companions on the road to the Vale.
thick as thieves.example: The two of them had grown thick as thieves since Chiggen had died.

out of hand.meaning: at once, without a trial or hearing
out of hand.here: They dare not simply kill Tyrion without justice; he is a Lannister of Casterly Rock.
out of hand.example: They dare not kill him out of hand; he was still a Lannister of Casterly Rock, and if they shed his blood, it would mean war.

under cover of night.here: Tywin sent Gregor to raid the riverlands without banners, hidden by darkness.
under cover of night.example: he’d taken care to see that he rode under cover of night, without banners

take the scent.meaning: to catch a smell and follow it
take the scent.here: The hounds caught the men's smell at the inn.
take the scent.example: That inn was full o’ them, and I saw them take the scent.

lay hands on.here: Tywin demands to know by what right Catelyn seized his son.
lay hands on.example: “By what right do you dare lay hands on my blood?”

come to pass.here: The crones say the Dothraki will one day gather as one people. It will happen.
come to pass.example: The crones have prophesied that one day that will come to pass, and so Vaes Dothrak must be ready

take ship.here: Ned thinks of sailing home to Winterfell by sea instead of riding the kingsroad.
take ship.example: Ned was no sailor, and ordinarily would have preferred the kingsroad, but if he took ship he could stop at Dragonstone and speak with Stannis Baratheon.

take pity.meaning: to feel sorry for someone and help them
take pity.here: In Tyrion's joke, the kind widow would feel sorry for the beggar and help him up.
take pity.example: Yet no doubt the gracious and compassionate widow would take pity, lift the poor unfortunate to his feet, and bless him with a gentle kiss of forgiveness.

take my part.meaning: to fight for me as my champion
take my part.here: Tyrion demands that someone fight for him in the trial by combat.
take my part.example: “And now I demand a champion, such as you have chosen for yourself. My brother Jaime will gladly take my part, I know.”

make short work of.here: Lysa's people think Ser Vardis will beat Bronn fast in the trial by combat.
make short work of.example: “Ser Vardis is a doughty fighter. He will make short work of the sellsword.”

make no mistake.here: Bronn warns Tyrion plainly. He fought for him, but he does not love him.
make no mistake.example: Make no mistake, dwarf. I fought for you, but I do not love you.”

make mock of.meaning: to make fun of; to laugh at
make mock of.here: Moon Boy mocks everyone cruelly at the feast, and no one is safe from his japes.
make mock of.example: His passion was a tragedy for all of us, but it was real, and pure, and nothing to be made mock of.

take a chill.meaning: to catch a cold from cold air or rain
take a chill.here: Ser Rodrik warns Catelyn to cover her head in the rain or she will catch cold.

took her breath away.here: The snowcapped mountains stunned Catelyn with their beauty.
took her breath away.example: snowcapped mountains that took her breath away.

look daggers.meaning: to stare at someone with hate
look daggers.here: Lysa stares angrily at her sister Catelyn.
look daggers.example: Still, her sister looked daggers at her.

steel kiss.meaning: a joking way to say a killing blow with a sword
steel kiss.here: Robert says to kiss the ugly woman and be done. Littlefinger jokes: kill her with a sword instead.

red smile.meaning: a cut throat; a wound across the neck that looks like a red smile
red smile.here: Tyrion jokes that his enemies would gladly slit his throat for him.
red smile.example: “If you wanted me dead, you had only to say the word, and one of these staunch friends of yours would gladly have given me a red smile.”

come of age.meaning: to become an adult; old enough to rule

come of age.example: “Lord Eddard Stark is herein named Protector of the Realm, to rule as regent until the heir comes of age.”

with child.here: Daenerys is carrying Khal Drogo's child, and the whole khalasar knows it.
forms: gotten a child on some girl

flower of your womanhood.meaning: the time when a girl becomes a woman and can marry

flower of your womanhood.example: when you come into the flower of your womanhood, you shall wed the king in the Great Sept of Baelor, before the eyes of gods and men.

play the game.meaning: to take part in court scheming and politics
play the game.here: Ned must scheme and hide his thoughts at court until he is safe enough to act.

tread softly.meaning: to act carefully so as not to cause trouble
tread softly.here: Ned must be cautious and quiet at court, hiding what he knows.
tread softly.example: The need for deceit was a bitter taste in his mouth, but Ned knew he must tread softly here, must keep his counsel and play the game until he was firmly established as regent.

keep his counsel.meaning: to keep your plans secret; to say nothing
keep his counsel.here: Ned must hide his thoughts and plans from the court.
keep his counsel.example: The need for deceit was a bitter taste in his mouth, but Ned knew he must tread softly here, must keep his counsel and play the game until he was firmly established as regent.

hold my tongue.meaning: to keep silent; not to speak
hold my tongue.here: Osha promises to stay quiet and wear her chains without protest.
hold my tongue.example: So be it. I’ll wear my irons and hold my tongue.

hold my water.here: The speaker would not wait around hoping for the man's thanks.
hold my water.example: but I wouldn’t hold my water waiting for his thanks, not that one.

turn your tail.meaning: to run away like a coward

turn your tail.example: If you turn your tail and retreat to Winterfell, your lords will lose all respect for you.

go over to.here: Some of Robb's lords may join the Lannisters if he looks weak.
go over to.example: Some may even go over to the Lannisters.

put them to flight.meaning: to make the enemy run away
put them to flight.here: Jaime scattered Edmure's men in battle.
put them to flight.example: "Uncle Edmure had sent Lord Vance and Lord Piper to hold the pass, but the Kingslayer descended on them and put them to flight.

put the spurs to.meaning: to kick your horse to make it gallop fast
put the spurs to.here: Ser Brynden rides quickly toward the banners.
put the spurs to.example: Ser Brynden Tully put the spurs to his horse and trotted briskly toward the banners.

put it out of my head.here: Tyrion can never forget the song the girl used to sing.
put it out of my head.example: The first girl I ever bedded used to sing it, and I’ve never been able to put it out of my head.”

bid her follow.meaning: to ask or order someone to come after you
bid her follow.here: The torchlight in the dark seemed to call Arya to follow it down the tunnel.
bid her follow.example: Long after their voices had faded away, Arya could still see the light of the torch, a smoking star that bid her follow.

await the pleasure.meaning: to wait until a great person is ready to see or judge you
await the pleasure.here: The poisoner must wait in chains for the khal's judgment.
await the pleasure.example: “Take this one away to await the pleasure of the khal,” he commanded, gesturing at the man on the ground.
forms: await the pleasure of the khal

if truth be told.here: The speaker honestly admits he is not sure what the Imp really is.
if truth be told.example: Now, if truth be told, I’m not sure what he is.

it makes no matter.here: Chicken, duck, or pigeon, any roast bird will do for Tyrion.

as good as buried.meaning: certain to die; as good as dead
as good as buried.here: A Faceless Man would surely have killed Daenerys by now.
as good as buried.example: If we'd sent a Faceless Man after her, she'd be as good as buried.

make him fly.meaning: to throw someone out of the Moon Door to their death
make him fly.here: Little Robert Arryn eagerly wants to see Tyrion thrown out of the Moon Door.

take up steel.meaning: to take up weapons and fight

take up steel.example: every man was expected to take up steel in its defense

lay down their swords.here: Cersei tells Ned to order his men to give up their weapons.
lay down their swords.example: “Tell your men to lay down their swords, and no one need—”

shed his blood.here: Killing Tyrion would mean war with the Lannisters, so they dare not.
shed his blood.example: if they shed his blood, it would mean war.

out of the mouth of babes.meaning: wise words spoken innocently by a child
out of the mouth of babes.here: Little Arya speaks a truth the grown-ups had missed.
out of the mouth of babes.example: Father looked at her strangely. “Gods,” he swore softly, “out of the mouth of babes…”

the back of beyond.here: Robert's anger would follow Cersei anywhere she fled, no matter how far.
the back of beyond.example: I promise you, no matter where you flee, Robert’s wrath will follow you, to the back of beyond if need be.”

see the back of.meaning: to be glad to leave a place
see the back of.here: Tom will not miss the Night's Watch when he leaves it.
see the back of.example: "Can't say I'll be sad to see the back of this place. I miss the wife."

take me for.meaning: to think I am; to mistake me for
take me for.here: Jon is angry that he is treated like a servant instead of a lord's son.
take me for.example: “Do you take me for a servant?”

take in hand.meaning: to take control of; to manage someone's upbringing

take in hand.example: "We must get Joffrey away from his mother and take him in hand.

die on me.meaning: to die and leave someone behind
die on me.here: Ned begs the dying Robert not to leave him alone.
die on me.example: "Robert," Ned said in a voice thick with grief, "you must not do this. Don't die on me. The realm needs you."

bear witness.meaning: to watch and confirm that something is true
bear witness.here: The gods are asked to watch the trial and judge the man's soul.
bear witness.example: “Hear my words, and bear witness to my vow,” they recited, their voices filling the twilit grove.

by rights.here: By law and justice, the man should already be dead.
by rights.example: "By rights, he should be dead already. I have never seen a man cling to life so fiercely."

in a body.here: The Watch's officers came together to the grove for the vows.
in a body.example: The high officers arrived in a body; Maester Aemon leaning on Clydas, Ser Alliser cold-eyed and grim, Lord Commander Mormont resplendent in a black wool doublet

in kind.meaning: in the same way; with the same treatment
in kind.here: Ned paid the man back the same way he had been treated.
in kind.example: Bastard did me good, eh? But I… I paid him back in kind, Ned.”

in heat.meaning: ready to mate, of a female animal
in heat.here: The mare was ready to breed, which made the stallion wild and hard to control.
in heat.example: "Tyrell had to know the mare was in heat," Littlefinger was saying.

on account of.here: Mya could not go back the way she came because of the monsters.
on account of.example: I couldn't go back the way I came on account of the monsters.

by turns.here: The dogs snarled, then whimpered, then snarled again, pulling at their leashes.
by turns.example: Even now they were snarling and whimpering by turns, pulling at their leashes while Chett cursed them for curs.

dead end.meaning: a place with no way out
dead end.here: The cellar stairs led nowhere. Arya was trapped with no escape.
dead end.example: The cellar was a dead end.

silence of the grave.here: After the fighting, the Red Keep was utterly silent.
silence of the grave.example: The fighting was over, and the silence of the grave had settled over the Red Keep.

hue and cry.meaning: a loud public alarm; a chase after a criminal
hue and cry.here: No one raised an alarm as Arya fled through the yard.
hue and cry.example: By the time she reached the shadow of the royal sept on the far side of the yard, Arya was cold with sweat, but no one had raised the hue and cry.

shadow of the axe.here: Ned sees his own death coming and cannot pretend otherwise.
shadow of the axe.example: I am not so blind that I cannot see the shadow of the axe when it is hanging over my own neck.

blood run black.meaning: to be dead; a dead man's blood runs black
blood run black.here: The wight's blood was black. He was a walking corpse.

beneath even his contempt.meaning: too low to even be worth despising
beneath even his contempt.here: Alliser Thorne thought bastards too low to even hate.
beneath even his contempt.example: Jon himself he had scarcely even noticed; bastards were beneath even his contempt.

feel it in my bones.meaning: to sense something deeply and surely
feel it in my bones.here: Mormont feels in his body that dark days are coming for the realm.
feel it in my bones.example: "This could not have happened at a worse time. If ever the realm needed a strong king… there are dark days and cold nights ahead, I feel it in my bones…"
forms: i feel it in my bones

none of our concern.here: The Night's Watch stays out of King's Landing politics.
none of our concern.example: “Whatever they do in King’s Landing is none of our concern.”

think the less of you.here: No one will blame or shame you for leaving the Watch now.
think the less of you.example: “Are there any among you who wish to leave our company? If so, go now, and no one shall think the less of you.”

take to him.here: The direwolf Ghost liked Sam immediately.
take to him.example: Ghost took to him straight off.

come to light.here: The truth about the queen and her children would soon be known to all.
come to light.example: That would come to light soon, as sure as sunrise, and with the king in such a black fury…

think better of it.meaning: to decide not to do something after all
